residual: P2: `test_an_anchor_embedded_in_prose_does_not_claim_another_section` cannot fail on the defect its name describes: it passes identically with the pre-fix unanchored `_IDENTITY_RE`. I measured this by monkeypatching the old pattern back in-process — the intruder record's fingerprint differs from the first record's under both regexes, so `place_escalation_section` appends either way and the assertions (2 sections, `## [s2]` present, first anchor kept) hold with and without the fix. The two sibling tests added in the same hunk ARE genuine guards: with the old regex `test_a_legacy_section_quoting_an_anchor_is_left_standing` yields 1 section instead of 2 and loses the older render, and `test_a_section_carrying_only_an_embedded_anchor_has_no_identity` gets the fingerprint back instead of "". So the fix is covered; this third test is a non-falsifying assertion whose name claims regression protection it does not provide, which the run's rule on tautological assertions targets.

P3: Implementer concern, verified: `self.assertLess(SHIPPED_SHIM_LINES, mc.MAX_SHIM_LINES)` compares two module-level constants (2 and 5) and can only change on a deliberate edit to one of them — no product-source change can move it. It is not strictly tautological (a maintainer lowering MAX_SHIM_LINES to 2 would trip it), and its own docstring discloses the limitation in those words, so it does not over-claim. My judgment on the run's cardinal rule: acceptable as shipped, because the falsifiable assertion sits two lines below it and the docstring narrows the claim rather than inflating it. Recorded so the decision is on the record rather than left implicit.

P2: Two of the four new pure helper functions added in this diff carry the repo's '(PURE)' docstring marker (resolve_main_shim, resolve_omit) while the other two equally pure helpers (_sole_shim_header, _guarded_block) do not — and this file had zero '(PURE)' markers anywhere before this diff (confirmed by grep over all ~15 pre-existing clearly-pure functions such as executable_lines, normalize_key, apply_omit, parse_omit), so the marker is being introduced piecemeal and inconsistently rather than following either this file's own prior style or a uniform rule within the new code itself.

P3: _guarded_block's trailing-blank-line trim is a two-pass approach: it first grows `resolved` forward through every line (blank or not) up to the next column-zero line, then repeatedly recomputes max(resolved) and discards it while that line is blank. A single forward scan that tracks the index of the last non-blank line seen, then builds the final range from `start` to that index, would express the same result without the repeated max()-over-a-set lookups. This exact simplification was already flagged as a residual P3 in the prior review round's package (s12-fix1.md) and remains unaddressed in the shipped diff.
